title: Module sheafification commutes with open localization
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $A$ a sheaf of rings on its open site, and $U$ an open. Let $V$ be restriction of sheaves of modules to the localized site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], $P$ sectionwise restriction of presheaves of modules to that site, and $a_A$ and $a_{A|_U}$ the module sheafification functors [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. For every presheaf of $A$-modules $M$, there is an isomorphism $V(a_A(M)) \cong a_{A|_U}(P(M))$, natural in $M$. Equivalently the two functors from presheaves of $A$-modules to sheaves of $A|_U$-modules are naturally isomorphic. No nonemptiness or nonzero coefficient assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03DH (sites-modules-section-localize), sectionwise localized restriction; Tag 03CY (sites-modules-lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules); restriction of the sheafification unit and the universal property

proof.text: Restrict the sheafification unit. Its underlying abelian-presheaf map is precomposition of the original sheafification unit by the forgetful functor from Over U. This functor is cocontinuous: coverings of W over U are exactly coverings of W, with forced maps to U. Hence the restricted unit is locally injective and locally surjective.

Use the localized module sheafification adjunction to extend this restricted unit to a module map from the sheafification of the restricted presheaf. Its composite with the localized unit is the restricted original unit. The localized unit is locally bijective, so cancellation makes the extended map locally bijective. A locally bijective map between sheaves of abelian groups is an isomorphism, and the functor forgetting module structures reflects isomorphisms.

The adjunction hom-equivalence and naturality of the original unit show the extended maps are natural in M. Their inverses form the desired natural isomorphism. The construction also applies to the empty open and zero rings.

theorem exists_open_localized_sheafification
    {X : TopCat.{u}} (A : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u})
    (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X) :
    let T := PresheafOfModules.sheafification.{u}
      (J := (Opens.grothendieckTopology X).over U) (R := A.over U)
      (𝟙 (A.over U).obj)
    Nonempty
      (PresheafOfModules.sheafification.{u} (R := A) (𝟙 A.obj) ⋙ overFunctor.{u} A U ≅
        PresheafOfModules.pushforward₀.{u} (Over.forget U) A.obj ⋙ T)
